question.problem: Find the equation of the tangent hyperplane to the hypersurface $w={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+xyz$ at the point $(1,1,1,1).$
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the hypersurface $w=f(x,y,z)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0},{w}_{0})$ on the hypersurface can be written as

$$
w-{w}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(z-{z}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂z}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+xyz)=2x+yz \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+xyz)=-2y+xz \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+xyz)=xy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y,z)=(1,1,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,1,1) & =2(1)+(1)(1)=3 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,1,1) & =-2(1)+(1)(1)=-1 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z}(1,1,1) & =(1)(1)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent hyperplane:

$$
\begin{aligned}w-1 & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,1,1)+(y-1)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,1,1)+(z-1)\frac{∂f}{∂z}(1,1,1) \\ w-1 & =3(x-1)-(y-1)+(z-1) \\ w-1 & =3x-3-y+1+z-1 \\ -3x+y-z+w+2 & =0 \\ 3x-y+z-w-2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
